chunks: And 'Abdullah ibn Muskān narrated from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, who said:

I asked Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) about two men who had wealth, part of which was in their possession and part of which was scattered/absent from them. They divided equally what was in their possession and what was absent. Then, the share of one of them was lost from what was absent from him, while the other received his share in full. I asked: Should he return [compensate] to his partner? He said: 'Yes, so that he does not take all the wealth for himself.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on compensating a partner when one loses their share of absent wealth while the other receives theirs in full?
ai.summary: This narration from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* clarifies the principle of *al-kaff* (compensation) in joint ownership, where the partner who successfully recovers the absent share must return the surplus to the other to equalize their holdings. It underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on equitable risk-sharing, ensuring that the benefit of recovery is not retained exclusively by one party when the initial division was based on equality.
